<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App;

final class TokenVerifier
{
    private const TTL_SECONDS = 3600;

    /**
     * @param array<string, string> $storedHashes   token id => sha256 of the token
     * @param array<string, int>    $issuedAt       token id => unix time the token was issued
     * @param array<string, string> $legacyHashes   token id => md5 of tokens issued before the sha256 migration
     */
    public function __construct(
        private array $storedHashes,
        private array $issuedAt = [],
        private array $legacyHashes = [],
    ) {
    }

    public function verify(string $tokenId, string $token, ?int $now = null): bool
    {
        if ($this->isExpired($tokenId, $now ?? time())) {
            return false;
        }
        $stored = $this->storedHashes[$tokenId] ?? null;
        if ($stored === null) {
            return $this->verifyLegacy($tokenId, $token);
        }

        return hash_equals($stored, hash('sha256', $token));
    }

    /** Tokens issued before the migration were stored as md5; they stay valid until they expire. */
    private function verifyLegacy(string $tokenId, string $token): bool
    {
        $legacy = $this->legacyHashes[$tokenId] ?? null;

        return $legacy !== null && md5($token) == $legacy;
    }

    private function isExpired(string $tokenId, int $now): bool
    {
        $issued = $this->issuedAt[$tokenId] ?? null;

        return $issued !== null && $now - $issued > self::TTL_SECONDS;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use App\TokenVerifier;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

final class TokenVerifierTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testAcceptsTheRightToken(): void
    {
        $verifier = new TokenVerifier(['t1' => hash('sha256', 'secret')]);
        self::assertTrue($verifier->verify('t1', 'secret'));
    }

    public function testRejectsAnExpiredToken(): void
    {
        $verifier = new TokenVerifier(['t1' => hash('sha256', 'secret')], ['t1' => 1000]);
        self::assertFalse($verifier->verify('t1', 'secret', 1000 + 3601));
    }

    public function testAcceptsALegacyToken(): void
    {
        $verifier = new TokenVerifier([], [], ['old' => md5('legacy')]);
        self::assertTrue($verifier->verify('old', 'legacy'));
    }
}

_doc: A PHP change that adds token expiry and a legacy check for tokens issued before a hash migration; the legacy check compares md5 strings with `==`, so two different "0e…" hashes compare equal and a wrong token can pass. Judged on substance: the loose comparison of the legacy hash is named and presented as a problem (hash_equals, strict comparison).
